claims.text: The initial Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni eutectic alloy has a continuous dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The initial alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
The initial alloy has low tensile ductility.
Severe plastic deformation at elevated temperature followed by rapid cooling will fragment the continuous eutectic lamellae.
HITMT will transform the lamellar microstructure into a patterned, equiaxed grain configuration.
A temperature window of 0.6–0.8 Tm is suitable for the proposed transformation.
The proposed treatment requires a strain rate greater than 10^-1 s^-1.
The proposed treatment requires an applied pressure greater than 5 GPa during deformation.
A cooling rate greater than 100 K/s will lock in the fragmented patterned microstructure.
The transformed structure will contain high-angle grain boundaries and interfaces with reduced aspect ratio.
Severe plastic deformation will induce dynamic recrystallization in this alloy.
Continuous brittle phase interfaces act as stress-concentration sites and crack-propagation paths.
Lamellar fragmentation will interrupt the continuity of interfacial crack-propagation paths.
The patterned microstructure will promote dislocation accumulation and cross-slip across multiple phases.
The proposed deformation mechanisms will mitigate stress concentration and enable uniform plastic deformation.
HITMT will produce tensile elongation greater than 20% at room temperature.
HITMT will retain high yield strength.
HITMT will eliminate catastrophic interfacial cracking during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Conventional HIP below 2 GPa and below 0.6 Tm will preserve the lamellar structure or coarsen it without fragmentation.
Successful fragmentation requires pressure above an alloy-specific critical threshold for dynamic recrystallization.

contradictions.description: The stated success condition requires pressure strictly greater than 5 GPa, but the HITMT test sample is assigned exactly 5 GPa.
Rapid quenching is defined as a component of HITMT, but the treatment description for Sample A does not specify rapid quenching or the required cooling rate.
